newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Budapest leads E. Europe stocks on all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest leads E. Europe stocks on all-time high.

text.p: An all-time high on the Budapest stock exchange and gains in Bucharest and Ljubljana combined to help save what could have been a week of losses on East European markets.
The rise in Budapest, following a trading high on Tuesday and a slide on Thursday, was seen as a result of foreign capital inflows leaving the ailing Czech market.
A weaker local currency lent turbulence to the Czech market and pulled Warsaw lower. The volatile crown in Bratislava drove volume and turnover to year lows and in Croatia shares traded mixed.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which measures price movements in 72 Hungarian, Polish, Czech, Slovak and Slovenian stocks, fell 1.74 percent.
PRAGUE
Czech shares had a turbulent week as the Czech central bank was forced to allow a depreciation of the crown and a reshuffled government announced new austerity measures.

On Tuesday, when the crown depreciated by around 10 percent versus the dollar and mark, the PX50 posted its biggest gain for over three years. But the bull run was short-lived with analysts citing concerns about the economy as a whole.

The Czech PX50 index fell back again on Friday but a combative speech from Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus in the afternoon pledging to fight on to reform the economy was received well by dealers, who said it could renew faith in the ailing equities market.
WARSAW

The Warsaw bourse fell this week due to zloty falls triggered by the Czech crown slump and a busy primary market, but analysts expected it to maintain the almost 2.5-month horizontal trend on the longer term.

They said they expected no major selling or buying at the current prices. If the zloty stabilises after a two-percent fall since Thursday last week the bourse might rise moderately in the next sessions, they said.

Analysts said strong gains were unlikely as Poland's largest commercial Bank Handlowy SA share offering worth one billion zlotys and copper giant KGHM's offer, expected in in July, were drawing capital from the bourse.
BUDAPEST
A sudden rally on the Budapest stock exchange on Friday helped the BUX index to close at an all-time high of 6,018.11 points, up 144.52 from last Friday.
Traders attributed the sudden rise to an inflow of fresh funds to the Budapest bourse, which seems to be one of the new destinations of money leaving the troubled Czech markets.
However, analysts still predicted a sideways trend on the market on the short term.
BRATISLAVA
Political and economic instability worked in tandem to paralyse activity on the Bratislava Stock Exchange this week, highlighted by a year lows in overall volume and turnover in Thursday's session.
The official 16-share SAX index eased 1.97 points, or 1.01 percent from Monday's open to close at 193.55 on Friday.

Brokers said investors took flight from the market mainly due to a turbulent money market and the volatile Slovak crown, but also because of fallout from plebiscites on NATO membership and direct presidential elections which were declared void.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares rose 0.37 percent this week, as the blue-chip SBI index climbed 4.86 points to 1,323.33.
Traders said future moves on the market would largely depend on the ratification of the EU association accord, signed last June. Parliament is due to vote within the next two weeks.
Traders said the ratification could push up the blue- chip index by as much as 30 percent in up to three months as foreign investors resumed buying and market liquidity increased.
If the ratification fails, shares could fall by up to 30 percent before end-summer, they forecast.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks ended the week mixed ahead of a public holiday with Zagrebacka Banka forging ahead on stronger volume.

The bank recouped its recent losses to close at 2,100 kuna with 3,875 shares sold. Its GDRs in London also rose strongly after the bank announced it struck a deal with foreign creditors on a loan for a minimum 300 million marks.
Traders expected the market to stay weak in little buying interest. They said foreign investors stood back given Western political pressures on Croatia and too expensive stock prices.
BUCHAREST
The Bucharest stock exchange, which performed poorly early in the week, recovered its poise on Thursday and entered a rally on Friday when most shares closed higher.
Volume rose to 2.5 million shares from 2.3 million and turnover climbed by some 840 million lei to 7.5 billion.
The first tier dominated the market in thinner early-week trading and on Friday, when it took 80 percent of turnover.
